profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CyrusOne campus sits in Loudoun County, Virginia, in and around Sterling, part of the Northern Virginia Ashburn area data center corridor. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company purchased 40 acres in Loudoun County in June 2016 for data center construction. CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, went public in 2013, and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne NVA4 publishes 11 MW of IT capacity across 128,715 square feet of technical space in Sterling, Virginia. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 11 MW supports roughly 275 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, the same power supports roughly 1,100 racks. The operator has not published certifications for this campus, so no certification-based qualification for regulated or sensitive workloads can be read from the available data.

Eleven megawatts is a modest figure relative to hyperscale AI infrastructure. Among the five Virginia facilities this site has read published MW figures for, NVA4 ranks fifth, the smallest by that measure, against a published state total of 233 MW across those five campuses. Virginia has 326 facilities mapped in OpenStreetMap, and only five have published capacity figures here, so 11 MW should be understood as NVA4's share of a very incomplete picture of the state.

Northern Virginia is the densest data center market in the world by most industry accounts, but that context comes from outside the data provided here. What the data show is that NVA4 sits in Sterling, close to the core of that corridor, at a scale that fits an enterprise or mid-market colocation use case more readily than it fits a large AI training cluster. A single large GPU pod at current frontier densities could consume its entire published capacity. Whether the campus has expansion rights, additional power commitments, or named AI tenants is not published.
